learn.rule: Because tells the reason. But shows a surprise or a difference. So tells the result.
learn.ruleEs: Because dice la razón. But muestra una sorpresa o una diferencia. So dice el resultado.
learn.model: The ice cube melted quickly because the sun warmed the sidewalk.
learn.notice: Look at the word because. What comes after it? The reason the ice melted.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word because in this melting sentence?
items.text: The ice cube melted quickly on the sidewalk because

options.text: the sun had warmed the concrete.

items.why: Because is followed by the reason. The warm concrete explains why the ice melted.
items.whyEs: Because va seguido de la razón. El cemento tibio explica por qué se derritió el hielo.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word but in this magnet sentence?
items.text: The magnet picked up the steel paper clip, but

options.text: Mia put the clips back in the box.
it could not lift the plastic spoon.

items.why: But shows a surprise or a difference. The magnet worked on steel and did not work on plastic.
items.whyEs: But muestra una sorpresa o una diferencia. El imán funcionó con el acero y no con el plástico.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word so in this toy car sentence?
items.text: The battery in the toy car was dead, so

options.text: we put in a new battery.
the toy was a birthday gift.

items.why: So tells the result. A dead battery leads to a new battery.
items.whyEs: So dice el resultado. Una batería agotada lleva a poner una batería nueva.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word that makes sense for the frog sentence.
items.model: Frogs lay eggs in water because their eggs must stay wet.
items.why: The second part gives the reason frogs lay eggs in water, so because is the best fit.
items.whyEs: La segunda parte da la razón por la que las ranas ponen huevos en el agua, así que because encaja mejor.

items.prompt: Choose a joining word for each blank in this winter morning story.
parts: The temperature dropped below zero degrees Celsius,
the puddles turned to ice. The sun came out,
the ice stayed hard until noon.
items.model: The temperature dropped below zero degrees Celsius, so the puddles turned to ice. The sun came out, but the ice stayed hard until noon.
items.why: The cold caused the ice, so we use so. The sun should melt ice, which is a surprise, so we use but.
items.whyEs: El frío causó el hielo, así que usamos so. El sol debería derretir el hielo, y eso es una sorpresa, así que usamos but.

items.prompt: Check every ending that fits the word but in this moon sentence.
items.text: The moon looks bright at night, but

options.text: many people enjoy watching it rise.
it makes no light of its own.
its dusty rocks are really dark gray.
we can see it from the backyard.

items.why: But needs a surprise. The moon looks bright, yet it makes no light of its own and its surface is really dark gray.
items.whyEs: But necesita una sorpresa. La luna se ve brillante, pero no produce luz propia y su superficie es en realidad gris oscuro.

write.prompt: Finish the stem three ways: once with because, once with but, and once with so.
write.promptEs: Termina la frase de tres maneras: una con because, una con but y una con so.
write.model: Magnets are useful because they hold notes on the refrigerator. Magnets are useful, but they only attract some metals. Magnets are useful, so engineers put them inside speakers.

familyTalk.en: At dinner, finish this three ways: 'We wear coats ...' with because, but, and so.
familyTalk.es: En la cena, terminen esto de tres maneras: 'Nos ponemos abrigos ...' con because, but y so.

teacherTip.en: Have pairs say all three versions aloud before writing so the meaning of each joining word is clear.
teacherTip.es: Pide que las parejas digan las tres versiones en voz alta antes de escribir, para que el significado de cada palabra quede claro.

learn.rule: Because tells the reason. But shows a surprise or a difference. So tells the result.
learn.ruleEs: Because dice la razón. But muestra una sorpresa o una diferencia. So dice el resultado.
learn.model: Merchants traveled in caravans because a group was safer than traveling alone.
learn.notice: What comes after because? The reason the merchants traveled together.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word because in this Silk Road sentence?
items.text: Merchants on the Silk Road traveled in large caravans because

options.text: it was safer to travel in a group.

items.why: Because gives the reason. Traveling together made the long trip safer.
items.whyEs: Because da la razón. Viajar juntos hacía el largo viaje más seguro.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word but in this desert sentence?
items.text: The Gobi Desert was hot in summer, but

options.text: travelers brought water in leather bags.
it could be freezing cold in winter.

items.why: But shows a difference. Hot summers and freezing winters are opposites.
items.whyEs: But muestra una diferencia. Los veranos calurosos y los inviernos helados son opuestos.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word so in this trade sentence?
items.text: Few merchants traveled the whole route from China to Rome, so

options.text: goods passed from trader to trader along the way.

items.why: So tells the result. Because no one made the whole trip, goods were handed on from trader to trader.
items.whyEs: So dice el resultado. Como nadie hacía todo el viaje, las mercancías pasaban de comerciante en comerciante.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word that fits the glass sentence.
parts: buyers there wanted to purchase it.
items.model: Traders carried glass to China because buyers there wanted to purchase it.
items.why: The second part tells why traders carried glass, so because is the best fit.
items.whyEs: La segunda parte dice por qué los comerciantes llevaban vidrio, así que because encaja mejor.

items.prompt: Choose a joining word for each blank in this caravan story.
parts: travelers wore thick wool cloaks. The trip took months,
many merchants made it again and again.
items.model: The desert nights were cold, so travelers wore thick wool cloaks. The trip took months, but many merchants made it again and again.
items.why: Cold nights led to warm cloaks, so we use so. A very long trip is a reason to stop, so repeating it is a surprise and needs but.
items.whyEs: Las noches frías llevaron a usar capas abrigadas, así que usamos so. Un viaje muy largo es motivo para parar, así que repetirlo es una sorpresa y necesita but.

items.prompt: Check every ending that fits the word so in this oasis sentence.
items.text: Many caravans stopped at oasis towns, so

options.text: the Gobi covers a very large area.
merchants could trade goods there too.

items.why: So tells what happened as a result. Stopping at an oasis meant water and a place to trade.
items.whyEs: So dice lo que pasó como resultado. Parar en un oasis significaba tener agua y un lugar para comerciar.

write.prompt: Finish the stem three ways: once with because, once with but, and once with so.
write.promptEs: Termina la frase de tres maneras: una con because, una con but y una con so.
write.text: Camels were important on the Silk Road
write.frame: Camels were important on the Silk Road ___
write.model: Camels were important on the Silk Road because they could carry heavy loads. Camels were important on the Silk Road, but they still needed rest and care. Camels were important on the Silk Road, so merchants bought them for the desert crossing.

familyTalk.en: Ask: 'Why do people travel in groups?' Answer with because, then change it with but and so.
familyTalk.es: Pregunten: '¿Por qué viaja la gente en grupo?' Respondan con because y luego cámbienlo con but y so.

teacherTip.en: Draw three arrows on the board (reason, surprise, result) and have students point to the right arrow for each model sentence.
teacherTip.es: Dibuja tres flechas en la pizarra (razón, sorpresa, resultado) y pide que los estudiantes señalen la flecha correcta para cada oración modelo.

sets.title: Rainy Day Plans
sets.titleEs: Planes para un día de lluvia

learn.rule: Because tells the reason. But shows a surprise or a difference. So tells the result.
learn.ruleEs: Because dice la razón. But muestra una sorpresa o una diferencia. So dice el resultado.
learn.model: The soccer game was canceled because lightning flashed over the field.
learn.notice: The words after because explain why the game was canceled.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word because in this soccer sentence?
items.text: The soccer game was canceled because
items.why: Because needs a reason. Lightning is a good reason to cancel a game.
items.whyEs: Because necesita una razón. Los relámpagos son una buena razón para cancelar un partido.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word but in this spelling test sentence?
items.text: Amara studied for the spelling test all week, but
items.why: But shows a surprise. We expect a student who studies to do well, so missing words is unexpected.
items.whyEs: But muestra una sorpresa. Esperamos que quien estudia le vaya bien, así que fallar palabras es inesperado.

items.prompt: Which ending fits the word so in this library sentence?
items.text: The library closed early for the holiday, so

options.text: the librarian wears a blue scarf.
we returned our books the next day.

items.why: So tells the result. The library was closed, so the books went back another day.
items.whyEs: So dice el resultado. La biblioteca estaba cerrada, así que los libros se devolvieron otro día.

items.prompt: Choose the joining word that fits the raincoat sentence.
items.model: Marcus put on his raincoat because the sky looked stormy.
items.why: The sky looking stormy is the reason for the raincoat, so because fits.
items.whyEs: El cielo con aspecto de tormenta es la razón del impermeable, así que because encaja.

items.prompt: Choose a joining word for each blank in this bus story.
parts: we waited inside the library. We were tired,
items.model: The bus was late, so we waited inside the library. We were tired, but we still sang songs together.
items.why: A late bus led to waiting inside, so we use so. Being tired and singing anyway is a surprise, so we use but.
items.whyEs: El autobús tarde llevó a esperar adentro, así que usamos so. Estar cansados y aun así cantar es una sorpresa, así que usamos but.

items.prompt: Check every ending that fits the word because in this violin sentence.
items.text: Jada practiced her violin every day because

options.text: she wanted to play in the school concert.
her teacher said practice builds skill.

items.why: Because needs a reason for the practice. Wanting to perform and building skill both explain it.
items.whyEs: Because necesita una razón para practicar. Querer tocar en el concierto y mejorar la habilidad lo explican.

write.prompt: Finish the stem three ways: once with because, once with but, and once with so.
write.promptEs: Termina la frase de tres maneras: una con because, una con but y una con so.
write.text: Our class held a bake sale
write.frame: Our class held a bake sale ___
write.model: Our class held a bake sale because we wanted to raise money for the animal shelter. Our class held a bake sale, but it started to rain. Our class held a bake sale, so many neighbors stopped by.

familyTalk.en: Tell about a plan that changed. Use 'We planned to ... but ...' and then 'so ...'.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten un plan que cambió. Usen 'Planeábamos ... but ...' y luego 'so ...'.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to explain why a wrong ending does not fit; naming the missing reason, surprise, or result builds the skill.
teacherTip.es: Pide que los estudiantes expliquen por qué un final incorrecto no encaja; nombrar la razón, la sorpresa o el resultado que falta fortalece la destreza.
